title: ICM 2026 Public Lectures - Terence Tao
summary: Terence Tao argues that AI is accelerating proof generation and verification in mathematics faster than humans can review, explain and absorb results, and calls for disclosure and new community norms.

assertions.quote: companies that are disclosing these have their own incentives to to maybe uh uh present the results in as favorable a light as possible

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: collectively they were able to sort of seven out of 10 at at publication level quality but at a non-trivial cost.

verdicts.note: Independent efforts like First Proof and Erdos-problem results show genuine solutions, though at high cost and on selected problems.

assertions.quote: proof review is now one of the most precious bottlenecks um scarce resources um in this new era.

verdicts.note: DORA and field reports show review and verification load growing with AI output, consistent with instability and persistent-debt findings.

The review's central synthesis is a 'verification gap': a mismatch between how fast AI workflows generate code and developers' capacity to verify it. This is an interpretive synthesis of mention-level evidence.
Google JUnit3->4 migration (5,359 files in 3 months): the bottleneck was how fast engineers could review, and change generation was deliberately throttled so reviewers were not overwhelmed.

AI users produced more, larger code but understood it less. Their median answering time was 3 min longer (+27%) and they switched back to the code more than twice as often, though the time effect was not robust. The authors suggest time saved may be offset later in the lifecycle.

assertions.quote: if an author cannot give a talk like up here about the result and they cannot take questions about the result

verdicts.note: Ownership and maintainability require understanding; it's a reasonable review standard rather than an empirical finding.

assertions.quote: it can be harmful to to to give students too much AI use early on.

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.

assertions.quote: we really need to normalize responsible disclosure of AI systems.

verdicts.note: A norm about research and engineering practice rather than a testable claim.
